text: This is what the LORD said: Go and buy a potter's earthenware jar. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests,
and go out to the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words I speak to you.

Say: Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring such disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.

For they have forsaken me and made this place foreign to me. They have burned incense here to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or spoke of, something that never entered my mind.
So look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will pour out and empty the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hand of those who seek their lives, and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

versions.text: In this place I will empty out the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hand of those who seek their lives, and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
versions.explanation: The verb baqqoti deliberately echoes the word for the jar (baqbuq) in verses 1 and 10. A slightly fuller rendering (or a footnote noting the wordplay between "jar" and "empty out") preserves the sound-link that drives the sign-act, which is especially valuable in oral reading.

text: I will make this city a horror, a thing to be hissed at; everyone who passes by will be appalled and will hiss at all its wounds.

I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they will devour one another's flesh in the siege and distress inflicted on them by their enemies and by those who seek their lives.
Then break the jar before the eyes of the men who go with you,

and say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: So will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel that can never be mended again. They will bury the dead in Topheth for lack of any other place to bury.

versions.text: and say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: So will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel that can never be mended again. And they will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no room left to bury.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מֵאֵין means "for lack of / because there is no," giving the reason burials happen in Topheth. "Until there is no room left" reverses the logic, implying burial there continues until space runs out rather than that Topheth is used because no other burial ground remains.

text: This is what I will do to this place and to those who live in it, declares the LORD. I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be defiled like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to the whole host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods.
Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the LORD's house and said to all the people:

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am bringing on this city and on all its surrounding towns every disaster I pronounced against it, because they stiffened their necks and refused to listen to my words.
